strings.P-32.hee1: The first Roombas had no map of the room; they cleaned the whole floor just by bumping into things and turning, over and over.
strings.P-33.name: Tower fan
strings.P-33.hee1: A bladeless fan really has blades inside its base, and the air coming out of the ring pulls the air around it along, making the flow many times bigger.
strings.P-34.name: Elevator
strings.P-34.hee1: Otis did not invent the elevator; what Otis made was a catch so that it "does not fall even if the rope breaks".
strings.P-35.name: Escalator
strings.P-35.hee1: The first escalator was a ride at an amusement park: a slanted moving belt, not stairs.
strings.P-36.name: Automatic door
strings.P-36.hee1: The automatic sliding door was born in a town where strong winds kept breaking swinging doors.
strings.P-37.name: City bus
strings.P-37.hee1: A turbo uses the push of the exhaust gas, which would have been thrown away, to force air into the engine.
strings.P-38.name: Mechanical wristwatch
strings.P-38.hee1: A mechanical wristwatch has no battery inside. It runs only on the power of its wound-up mainspring.
strings.I-01.name: Electromagnetic induction
strings.I-01.hee1: Electricity flows only "while you are moving" a magnet inside a coil. Stop, and it stops.
strings.I-02.name: Thermodynamics
strings.I-02.hee1: An engine's power depends not on "how hot" but on "the difference between the hot side and the cold side".
strings.I-03.name: Periodic table
strings.I-03.hee1: Mendeleev predicted the weight and properties of germanium before it had been found.
strings.I-04.name: Resolution limit of light
strings.I-04.hee1: With light, you cannot tell apart things finer than about half its wavelength. That is why the semiconductor world kept looking for "shorter light".
strings.I-05.name: Perceptron
strings.I-05.hee1: The first "learning machine" got smarter just by fixing itself a little each time it made a mistake.
strings.I-06.name: Segregation
strings.I-06.hee1: Sea ice has much less salt than the seawater around it. As it freezes, the salt is pushed out into the water that is left.
strings.I-07.name: How the electric arc works
strings.I-07.hee1: The hissing sound of an arc turned out to be carbon reacting with the oxygen in the air.
strings.I-08.name: Program
strings.I-08.hee1: Without rebuilding the machine, you can make it do a different job just by changing its list of steps (the program).
strings.I-09.name: Defining units by constants of nature
strings.I-09.hee1: One kilogram is no longer a lump in a vault; it is set by a "constant" that is the same anywhere in the universe.
strings.I-10.name: Logarithms
strings.I-10.hee1: A table of numbers that turns multiplication into addition.
strings.I-11.name: Creating accuracy without a reference
strings.I-11.hee1: The flattest plate can be made without an even flatter plate. Three plates are all you need.
strings.I-12.name: Three primary colors of light
strings.I-12.hee1: Look at a screen through a magnifying glass, and even the white parts are just tiny red, green and blue dots glowing.
strings.I-13.name: Separation of design and manufacturing
strings.I-13.hee1: The brain chip of a smartphone is often designed by one company and made in another company's factory.
strings.I-14.name: Standards
strings.I-14.hee1: A USB cable fits no matter where you bought it, because many companies follow the same rules.
strings.I-15.name: Patents and licensing
strings.I-15.hee1: A patent does not hide an invention; it is a promise of protection in return for making it public.
strings.I-16.name: Supply chain
strings.I-16.hee1: One smartphone holds materials taken from many different places around the world.
strings.I-17.name: CFCs and ozone depletion
strings.I-17.hee1: Because the countries of the world kept their promise and stopped using CFCs, the ozone layer is slowly starting to heal.
strings.I-18.name: Coandă effect
strings.I-18.hee1: Bring the back of a spoon close to water running from a tap, and the water is pulled toward the spoon. That is the Coandă effect.
strings.I-19.name: Diesel exhaust, air pollution and what is done about it
strings.I-19.hee1: Today's diesel buses have a filter that catches soot, and the soot it collects is burned off.
strings.I-20.name: Discovery of superconductivity
strings.I-20.hee1: Some metals, as they are cooled, suddenly lose everything that gets in the way of electricity flowing.
strings.I-21.name: Ionic theory and electrode potential
strings.I-21.hee1: Electricity flows through salt water because the salt splits into plus and minus particles in the water.
strings.I-22.name: Catalysts and surface chemistry
strings.I-22.hee1: A catalyst is still there after the reaction, without being used up.
strings.I-23.name: Macromolecular theory
strings.I-23.hee1: Inside plastic, tens of thousands of small molecules hold hands to make long chains.
strings.I-24.name: Discovery of oxygen and the theory of combustion
strings.I-24.hee1: Fire burns because the burning thing joins with the oxygen in the air.
strings.I-25.name: Discovery of the electron and the elementary charge
strings.I-25.hee1: Electricity is really made of tiny particles called "electrons", much smaller and lighter than atoms.
strings.I-26.name: Thermionic emission
strings.I-26.hee1: Inside a vacuum tube, electrons fly out of hot glowing metal like steam.
strings.I-27.name: Photoelectric effect and the photon
strings.I-27.hee1: Light is a wave, and also grains of energy of a fixed size.
strings.I-28.name: X-ray diffraction and crystal structure analysis
strings.I-28.hee1: Shine X-rays on a crystal, and the invisible arrangement of its atoms shows up as a pattern of dots.
strings.I-29.name: Band theory of solids
strings.I-29.hee1: A semiconductor is a material whose electrons sit right at the edge, needing just a little more energy to move.
strings.I-30.name: Noble gas compounds
strings.I-30.hee1: Even xenon, which was said to "react with nothing", joins with fluorine and its relatives.
strings.I-31.name: Laws of thermal radiation and the energy quantum
strings.I-31.hee1: The color inside a furnace goes from red to dazzling white because as it gets hotter, more light of short wavelengths comes out.
strings.I-32.name: Franck-Hertz experiment
strings.I-32.hee1: Atoms take in only exact, fixed amounts of energy.
strings.I-33.name: Tunneling in semiconductors
strings.I-33.hee1: Electrons sometimes slip through a thin wall they should not be able to cross.
strings.I-34.name: Superconducting tunneling and the quantum voltage standard
strings.I-34.hee1: The standard for "1 volt" is made with tiny superconducting devices and the frequency of microwaves.
strings.I-35.name: Quantum Hall effect
strings.I-35.hee1: The standard for "1 ohm" of electrical resistance is made with a cooled transistor and a magnet.
strings.I-36.name: Energy-based neural networks
strings.I-36.hee1: AI research uses ideas from the physics of heat and magnets.
strings.I-37.name: Giant magnetoresistance
strings.I-37.hee1: The read head of a hard disk has stacked films only a few dozen atoms thick.
strings.I-38.name: Van der Waals equation of state
strings.I-38.hee1: A squeezed gas shrinks less than you would expect, because molecules have a size too.
strings.I-39.name: Chemical equilibrium and chemical thermodynamics
strings.I-39.hee1: Ammonia plants use high pressure because the harder you push, the more the reaction moves toward ammonia.
strings.I-40.name: Radioactivity and transmutation of elements
strings.I-40.hee1: The helium in balloons was made by uranium in rocks underground over hundreds of millions of years.
strings.I-41.name: Chain reaction
strings.I-41.hee1: An explosion happens all at once because one reaction sets off two, then four, and so on.
strings.I-42.name: Characteristic X-rays and Moseley's law
strings.I-42.hee1: The order of the periodic table is set not by atomic weight but by the electric charge of the nucleus.
strings.I-43.name: Fermi–Dirac statistics
strings.I-43.hee1: Like a packed train, electrons can sit only one to a seat.
strings.I-44.name: Wave nature of electrons and electron diffraction
strings.I-44.hee1: Electrons are particles, yet they make diffraction patterns like waves.
strings.I-45.name: Quantum theory of chemical bonds
strings.I-45.hee1: In a silicon crystal, every atom holds hands with its four neighbors using its four hands.
strings.I-46.name: Computational chemistry
strings.I-46.hee1: New materials can now be searched for by computer calculation before any experiment is done.
strings.I-47.name: Quantum dots
strings.I-47.hee1: With the very same material, just making the grains smaller changes the color of the light.
strings.I-48.name: Onsager reciprocal relations
strings.I-48.hee1: Electricity made from a temperature difference, and electricity carrying heat, are the front and back of the same thing.
strings.I-49.name: The field of artificial intelligence
strings.I-49.hee1: The words "artificial intelligence" were first used in a 1955 proposal for a research workshop.
strings.I-50.name: Moore's law
strings.I-50.hee1: Moore's law is not a law of nature; it is more like a "promise" that the whole industry aimed for.
strings.I-51.name: Iron–carbon phase diagram and metallography
strings.I-51.hee1: Polish steel and look at it under a microscope, and you see different patterns depending on how much carbon it has.
strings.I-52.name: Dislocation theory
strings.I-52.hee1: Metals bend because "slips" in the arrangement of the atoms in the crystal move a little at a time.
strings.I-53.name: Abstraction
strings.I-53.hee1: A smartphone chip too is designed by stacking up "symbols" that bundle small circuits together, level upon level.
strings.I-54.name: Circuit symbols: drawing parts with fixed symbols and thinking in circuit diagrams
strings.I-54.hee1: Once you learn the symbols on a circuit diagram, you can read how electricity flows inside a machine without seeing the real thing.
strings.I-55.name: Zero moment point
strings.I-55.hee1: The way two-legged robots walk came from research on wearable robots to help people who cannot walk.
strings.I-56.name: Cancer caused by work
strings.I-56.hee1: In Britain long ago, children of about 8 swept chimneys, because they could fit inside the narrow flues.
strings.I-57.name: Isochronism of the pendulum
strings.I-57.hee1: A swing takes almost the same time for one back-and-forth whether you swing big or small.
strings.I-58.name: Hooke's law
strings.I-58.hee1: Hooke first announced the law he found as a code made by scrambling the letters.
strings.term.原子.name: atom
strings.term.原子.def: A very tiny particle that everything is made of. It has a nucleus in the middle and electrons around it.
strings.term.原子核.name: nucleus
strings.term.原子核.def: The very small, heavy center of an atom. It is made of protons (positive charge) and neutrons (no charge).
strings.term.電子.name: electron
strings.term.電子.def: A very light particle with negative charge that moves around an atom. When electrons flow, that is an electric current.
strings.term.元素.name: element
strings.term.元素.def: A kind of substance made of only one kind of atom, such as iron, copper or oxygen. They are lined up in the periodic table.
strings.term.分子.name: molecule
strings.term.分子.def: A particle made of a few atoms holding hands. A water molecule is two hydrogens and one oxygen.
strings.term.イオン.name: ion
strings.term.イオン.def: An atom or molecule with too many or too few electrons, so it carries a positive or negative charge.
strings.term.化合物.name: compound
strings.term.化合物.def: A substance made of two or more elements joined together, like salt (sodium chloride) or water.
strings.term.化学反応.name: chemical reaction
strings.term.化学反応.def: When substances join together or come apart and change into different substances.
strings.term.酸化.name: oxidation
strings.term.酸化.def: When something joins with oxygen (more widely, when it loses electrons). Iron rusting and things burning are both oxidation.
strings.term.還元.name: reduction
strings.term.還元.def: The opposite of oxidation: taking oxygen away from something (more widely, gaining electrons). It is used to get metals out of ores.
strings.term.合金.name: alloy
strings.term.合金.def: A metal mixed and melted together with other metals or elements, such as bronze (copper and tin) or steel (iron and carbon).
strings.term.結晶.name: crystal
strings.term.結晶.def: A solid in which atoms or molecules are packed tightly in a regular, repeating pattern. Salt, quartz and silicon wafers are crystals.
strings.term.単結晶.name: single crystal
strings.term.単結晶.def: A material that is one continuous crystal all the way through. Semiconductor chips are made from single-crystal silicon.
strings.term.半導体.name: semiconductor
strings.term.半導体.def: A material in between metals, which conduct electricity, and insulators, which do not. How well it conducts changes a lot with what is mixed in, with light, and with heat. Silicon and germanium are semiconductors.
strings.term.絶縁体.name: insulator
strings.term.絶縁体.def: A material that hardly conducts electricity at all, such as glass, rubber or plastic.
strings.term.導体.name: conductor
strings.term.導体.def: A material that conducts electricity well, such as metals like copper and aluminum.
strings.term.電流.name: electric current
strings.term.電流.def: The flow of electricity. Measured in amperes (A).
strings.term.電圧.name: voltage
strings.term.電圧.def: How strongly electricity is pushed to flow. Measured in volts (V).
strings.term.電気抵抗.name: electrical resistance
strings.term.電気抵抗.def: How hard it is for electricity to flow. Measured in ohms (Ω).
strings.term.電力.name: electric power
strings.term.電力.def: How much work electricity does in one second. Measured in watts (W).
strings.term.エネルギー.name: energy
strings.term.エネルギー.def: What lets things move, heat up or give off light. Measured in joules (J).
strings.term.温度.name: temperature
strings.term.温度.def: How hot or cold something is. It shows how hard the atoms and molecules inside are moving.
strings.term.圧力.name: pressure
strings.term.圧力.def: How strongly something pushes on a surface. Measured in pascals (Pa). The air pushes on the ground at about 100,000 pascals.
strings.term.真空.name: vacuum
strings.term.真空.def: A space with the air and other gases pumped out, so almost nothing is left.
strings.term.気体.name: gas
strings.term.気体.def: A state of matter, like air or steam, that has no fixed shape or size and spreads out.
strings.term.液体.name: liquid
strings.term.液体.def: A state of matter, like water, that has a fixed amount but takes the shape of its container.
strings.term.固体.name: solid
strings.term.固体.def: A state of matter, like stone or iron, that has a fixed shape and size.
strings.term.融点.name: melting point
strings.term.融点.def: The temperature at which a solid melts into a liquid. Ice melts at 0°C, iron at about 1538°C.
strings.term.沸点.name: boiling point
strings.term.沸点.def: The temperature at which a liquid boils into a gas. Water boils at 100°C (at 1 atmosphere of pressure).
strings.term.触媒.name: catalyst
strings.term.触媒.def: Something that speeds up a chemical reaction without changing itself.
strings.term.波長.name: wavelength
strings.term.波長.def: The distance from one crest of a wave to the next. The color of light depends on its wavelength, and shorter wavelengths can print finer patterns.
strings.term.周波数.name: frequency
strings.term.周波数.def: How many times a wave or vibration repeats in one second. Measured in hertz (Hz).
strings.term.電磁波.name: electromagnetic wave
strings.term.電磁波.def: A wave of electric and magnetic wobbles traveling along. Radio waves, infrared, light, ultraviolet and X-rays are all electromagnetic waves with different wavelengths.
strings.term.紫外線.name: ultraviolet
strings.term.紫外線.def: Light with a shorter wavelength than violet light, which our eyes cannot see. It is what causes sunburn.
strings.term.磁石.name: magnet
strings.term.磁石.def: Something that pulls iron toward it. It has a north pole and a south pole.
strings.term.磁場.name: magnetic field
strings.term.磁場.def: The space around a magnet or an electric current where magnetic force acts.
strings.term.不純物.name: impurity
strings.term.不純物.def: Something else mixed into a material. In semiconductors, a tiny amount is added on purpose to change how the material behaves.
strings.term.純度.name: purity
strings.term.純度.def: How free a material is from anything mixed in. "9N", nine nines in a row, means 99.9999999%.
strings.term.溶液.name: solution
strings.term.溶液.def: A liquid with something dissolved evenly in it, like salt water.
strings.term.酸.name: acid
strings.term.酸.def: A substance that tastes sour in water and can dissolve metals, like hydrochloric acid or sulfuric acid.
strings.term.アルカリ.name: alkali
strings.term.アルカリ.def: A substance with the opposite properties to an acid. Mix the two and they cancel each other out. Sodium hydroxide is an alkali.
strings.term.蒸留.name: distillation
strings.term.蒸留.def: Heating a liquid into vapor and cooling it back into liquid, to separate or purify things by their different boiling points.
strings.term.電気分解.name: electrolysis
strings.term.電気分解.def: Passing electricity through a liquid to split substances apart. You can get hydrogen and oxygen from water, or chlorine from salt water.
strings.term.同位体.name: isotope
strings.term.同位体.def: Atoms of the same element that have different numbers of neutrons in the nucleus, so they have different weights.
strings.term.放射線.name: radiation
strings.term.放射線.def: Invisible, high-energy particles or waves given off, for example, when an atomic nucleus breaks apart. Too much of it is bad for your body.
strings.term.回路.name: circuit
strings.term.回路.def: A path for electricity to flow along. A battery, wires and parts are connected into a loop.
strings.term.高分子.name: polymer
strings.term.高分子.def: A very long molecule made of thousands or tens of thousands of small molecules joined together. Plastics and rubber are polymers.
